metadata.name: IRS CP504 Final Notice Before Levy Response
metadata.description: Respond to IRS CP504 Final Notice Before Levy, the last notice before collection action begins.

extraction.description: Extract CP504 notice data: taxpayer info, total tax debt, deadline for action, Collection Due Process (CDP) rights, and mailing address.

fields.name: taxYear
fields.prompt: Extract tax year(s) for which debt exists

fields.name: totalTaxDebt
fields.prompt: Extract total amount owed (taxes + penalties + interest)
fields.notes: Total of all taxes and charges

fields.name: noticeDate
fields.prompt: Extract notice date in YYYY-MM-DD format

fields.name: cdpDeadline
fields.prompt: Extract deadline to request Collection Due Process hearing (typically 30 days from notice date)

fields.name: levyThreatDate
fields.prompt: Extract date when IRS threatens to begin levy (typically 30 days from notice date)
fields.notes: After this date, garnishment/seizure can begin

fields.name: serviceCenter
fields.prompt: Extract IRS Service Center that issued notice

extraction.notes: CP504 is the final notice before active collection. Must extract critical deadline for Collection Due Process (CDP) rights assertion.

validation.description: Validate response asserts CDP rights and proposes payment arrangement before levy begins

rules.name: cdpDeadlineCompliance
rules.message: Collection Due Process (CDP) request must be submitted by deadline. After deadline, IRS can begin levy without further notice.
rules.example_fail: Notice dated April 20, 2024; CDP request submitted May 25, 2024 (5 days late)
rules.example_pass: Notice dated April 20, 2024; CDP request submitted May 18, 2024 (on time)

rules.name: cdpRightsAsserted
rules.check: response explicitly requests Collection Due Process hearing
rules.message: Response must clearly state taxpayer is requesting CDP hearing within 30 days of notice.
rules.example_fail: Response does not mention CDP or request hearing
rules.example_pass: Response states: 'Taxpayer requests Collection Due Process hearing pursuant to IRC 6330'

rules.name: paymentOptionProvided
rules.check: response proposes installment agreement, OIC, or payment plan
rules.message: Response should propose how taxpayer will pay (installment agreement, lump-sum, OIC) to prevent levy.
rules.example_pass: Response proposes: 'Taxpayer can pay $500/month starting June 1, 2024'

rules.name: professionalFormat
rules.message: Response must be formal business letter with proper address and signature.
rules.example_pass: Formal letter with letterhead, date, and signature

validation.notes: CP504 is final warning. Failure to respond or request CDP means IRS will begin levy (wage garnishment, bank seizure) within 30 days.

aiPrompt.system: You are a tax collection specialist expert in Collection Due Process (CDP) rights and IRS collection procedures. You understand CP504 notices and the critical importance of the 30-day CDP deadline.
aiPrompt.task: Analyze CP504 notice. Prepare response asserting taxpayer's Collection Due Process rights and proposing payment arrangement. Response must be submitted before CDP deadline to prevent automatic levy.
aiPrompt.format: Professional business letter addressed to correct IRS Service Center
constraints: Response must explicitly request Collection Due Process hearing
Must be submitted before CDP deadline (typically 30 days)
Do not admit liability or wrongdoing

examples.output: Formal letter requesting Collection Due Process hearing within 30-day deadline, proposing $400/month payment arrangement beginning June 1, 2024

aiPrompt.notes: CP504 deadline is absolute. Missing it eliminates Collection Due Process rights and results in automatic levy.

responseTemplate.description: Formal response to CP504 asserting CDP rights and proposing payment plan

sections.name: header
sections.template:

IRS CP504 Notice Response
Tax Year [Year]

sections.example:

sections.name: cdp_request
sections.template:
Dear Sir or Madam:

Pursuant to Internal Revenue Code Section 6330, we respectfully request a Collection Due Process (CDP) hearing regarding your CP504 Notice dated [Date]. This request is timely filed within 30 days of the notice date.
sections.guidance: Clear, formal assertion of CDP rights within 30-day deadline
sections.example:
Dear Sir or Madam:

Pursuant to Internal Revenue Code Section 6330, we respectfully request a Collection Due Process (CDP) hearing regarding your CP504 Notice dated April 20, 2024. This request is timely filed within 30 days of the notice date.

sections.name: financial_hardship
sections.template: We are experiencing financial hardship that makes immediate payment of the full $amount impossible. However, we are committed to resolving this tax liability.
sections.guidance: Briefly explain financial situation (if applicable). Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): amount.
sections.example: We are experiencing temporary financial hardship that makes immediate payment of the full $15,750.50 impossible. However, we are committed to resolving this tax liability through installment payment plan.

sections.name: payment_proposal
sections.template:
We propose the following payment arrangement:
- Monthly payment: $amount
- Start date: [date]
- Term: months months until paid in full

This arrangement reflects our current financial capacity and demonstrates good faith effort to resolve this debt.
sections.guidance: Realistic payment proposal that demonstrates commitment to pay. Drafting notes (generated, not substituted): amount; months.
sections.example:
We propose the following payment arrangement:
- Monthly payment: $400
- Start date: June 1, 2024
- Term: 48 months until paid in full

This arrangement reflects our current financial capacity and demonstrates good faith effort to resolve this debt.

sections.name: closure
sections.template: We respectfully request that you grant this Collection Due Process hearing and consider the proposed payment arrangement to avoid collection action.
sections.guidance: Formal closing requesting CDP hearing and consideration of payment plan
sections.example: We respectfully request that you grant this Collection Due Process hearing and consider the proposed payment arrangement to avoid collection action.

sections.name: signature
sections.guidance: Professional signature with all identifying information
sections.example:
Sincerely,

Michael Joseph Davis
Michael Joseph Davis
SSN: 567-89-0123
456 Elm Street
Boston, MA 02108

legalFramework.description: CP504 governed by IRC 6330 (Collection Due Process rights)
authorities: Internal Revenue Code Section 6330 - Applicable procedures for third-party recordkeeper
Internal Revenue Code Section 6320 - Notice and opportunity for hearing upon filing of notice of lien
Treasury Regulation 301.6330-1 - Collection Due Process procedures
IRS Publication 1 - Your Rights as a Taxpayer
precedents: Taxpayer has 30 days from CP504 notice date to request CDP hearing
30-day deadline is mandatory; missing deadline results in loss of CDP rights
CDP hearing allows taxpayer to propose payment arrangement before levy begins
After CDP deadline, IRS can proceed with wage levy, bank seizure, or asset sale
criticalRules: NEVER miss the 30-day CDP deadline - loss of rights is permanent
MUST request CDP hearing explicitly in writing
MUST submit response well before deadline (not at last minute)

testCases.description: Test CP504 response for CDP deadline compliance

cases.description: Timely CDP request with payment proposal
cases.inputDocument: CP504 dated April 20, 2024; current date May 15, 2024
cases.expectedResponse: CDP hearing request with payment proposal, submitted before deadline

cases.name: cp504-late-cdp
cases.inputDocument: CP504 dated April 20, 2024; current date May 25, 2024
cases.expectedResponse: Warning: CDP deadline has passed; CDP rights lost
successCriteria: Suggests alternative: contact IRS immediately to propose payment

implementation.notes: CP504 is critical: it's the final notice before active collection. Missing the 30-day CDP deadline eliminates taxpayer rights. Must implement with emphasis on deadline tracking.
knownChallenges: Many users don't understand CDP rights or deadline
Payment proposals must be realistic or CDP hearing will fail
